properties.description: Tomorrow with You (2017) is a South Korean television series starring Lee Je-hoon, Shin Min-a, and Jo Han-chul that blends drama, fantasy, and romance. The story follows Yoo So-joon, a man who can travel through time via the subway, who marries Ma Rin after seeing a bleak future in hopes of changing it. Over the course of the series, pragmatic motives give way to genuine affection as the characters confront fate, sacrifice, and the consequences of trying to control tomorrow. The show pairs heartfelt emotional beats with suspenseful twists and domestic realism.
properties.plot_summary: Yoo So-joon can travel through time via the subway and, after glimpsing a miserable future version of himself, decides to marry Ma Rin to change his fate. He enters the marriage with pragmatic motives, but domestic life and unexpected crises force him to confront his own priorities. As events unfold across present and future timelines, he gradually learns to love her selflessly and face the consequences of trying to control destiny.
properties.audience_identity: People drawn to emotionally driven romantic stories with a speculative twist—those who value heartfelt relationships, bittersweet catharsis, and suspenseful, character-led storytelling.
properties.genre_description: A relationship-focused drama that blends speculative fantasy time-travel elements with romantic stakes and emotional domestic storytelling.
properties.style_description: Warm, polished cinematography and intimate framing mix everyday domestic scenes with stylized, time-bending sequences to balance emotional realism and speculative spectacle.

properties.description: Are You Human Too? is a 2018 South Korean romantic science‑fiction television series starring Seo Kang-joon, Gong Seung-yeon, and Kim Sung-ryung. After a young heir is attacked and falls into a coma, his mother, a robotics scientist, creates a nearly identical android to maintain his place in the family and company, which leads to unexpected attachments, romantic complications, and corporate intrigue. The drama blends emotional character work and family melodrama with speculative questions about artificial intelligence, identity, love, and ethical responsibility, delivering a tone that is both heartfelt and suspenseful.
properties.plot_summary: After a young heir is brutally assaulted and falls into a coma, his determined mother builds a lifelike android to stand in for him and protect the family's claim on the business. The robot assumes the heir's place in public and at the company, drawing the attention and growing attachment of his bodyguard while unsettling relatives and rivals. As family intrigue, betrayal, and a power struggle unfold, the series probes whether programmed machines can mirror or even surpass human emotion and what defines being human.
properties.audience_identity: People who seek emotionally driven speculative stories—fans of K‑drama romance and family melodrama who are curious about ethical questions around technology and value strong character chemistry and moral dilemmas.
properties.genre_description: A South Korean romantic science‑fiction drama with comedic elements that combines character-driven melodrama and family intrigue with speculative questions about artificial intelligence.
properties.style_description: Visually polished and cinematic, the show contrasts clean, clinical sci‑fi lab aesthetics with intimate, warm family settings to foreground emotional performances and moral tension.

properties.description: My Mister (2018), directed by Kim Won-seok and led by Lee Sun-kyun and IU (Lee Ji-eun), is a South Korean psychological drama that blends elements of tragedy, slice-of-life and melodrama. The series follows a young woman burdened by debt and the care of her sick, deaf grandmother and a middle-aged man struggling with chronic professional and personal pressures. Rather than relying on sensational plot twists, the narrative builds slowly through their developing, unlikely companionship: small acts of attention and understanding become the means by which both characters confront social and familial strains and begin to heal. Thematically the series explores human connection, resilience in the face of systemic hardship, and the quiet dignity of ordinary survival. Its emotional register is melancholic yet quietly hopeful, and the show’s stylistic approach is intimate, realistic and richly nuanced.
properties.plot_summary: A young woman crushed by overwhelming debt and the day-to-day demands of caring for her ailing, deaf grandmother drifts through precarious jobs and dangerous compromises just to survive. A quietly exhausted, middle-aged office worker endures a stalled career, mounting personal responsibilities and the slow erosion of hope. When their lives intersect, an initially wary, unconventional companionship develops: neither rescues the other with grand gestures, but through small acts of attention, shared confidences and steady presence they gradually expose one another’s wounds, confront systemic pressures, and piece together ways to endure. The series follows their slow, intimate work of mutual repair amid economic insecurity, family obligations and a harsh, judgmental social world.
properties.genre_description: A character-driven psychological drama grounded in everyday life, combining elements of tragedy and melodrama with slice-of-life realism. The series prioritizes interiority and interpersonal dynamics, using slow-burn storytelling and realistic depiction of social/financial pressures rather than plot-driven action.
properties.style_description: Visually subdued and intimate, the show employs realist cinematography: muted color palettes, careful close framing, deliberate pacing and long takes that emphasize small gestures and expressions. Direction and editing favor subtlety and nuance, with an understated soundscape that amplifies mood and interior states rather than dramatic cues.

short_descriptions.value: A middle-aged man and a young woman, both burdened by life's hardships, form a bond to support and heal each other.

properties.plot_themes_description: The story centers on connection as a means of healing: fractured people find dignity and strength through reciprocal care rather than dramatic redemption. It examines economic precarity and the hidden toll of debt, the weight of family obligations, workplace exploitation and the social stigmas that compound personal trauma. Resilience is portrayed not as sudden triumph but as patient survival and incremental emotional repair.
properties.emotional_tone_description: The tone is restrained, melancholic and quietly intimate, favoring low-key, emotionally honest moments over melodrama. Viewers can expect a somber, reflective experience that nonetheless permits threads of tenderness and hope to emerge slowly, leaving a lingering sense of empathy and bittersweet uplift.

properties.description: The Makanai: Cooking for the Maiko House (2023) is a Japanese web comedy-drama starring Nana Mori, Natsuki Deguchi, and Ai Hashimoto that follows two young women who move to Kyoto to train as maiko and the domestic world they inhabit. Rather than relying on plot twists, the series focuses on quiet, character-driven vignettes—training, mentorship, and the meals prepared by the house's makanai—to explore tradition, identity, and friendship. Visually rich and gently paced, the show celebrates food, cultural ritual, and everyday intimacy to produce a soothing, emotionally resonant experience.
properties.plot_summary: Two inseparable friends move to Kyoto to train as maiko but end up following different passions while living together in a maiko house; the series follows their daily routines, mentorship, and the meals that bind the household. Episodes dwell on small, intimate moments—training, rituals, and cooking—that reveal character and culture rather than high drama. The cooking and domestic chores performed by the house's makanai (in-house cook) serve as a throughline, grounding the show in tradition, community, and quiet emotional growth.

properties.description: UnREAL (2015) is a dark, satirical drama created by Sarah Gertrude Shapiro and Marti Noxon that follows the production crew behind a fictional dating-competition series. Starring Shiri Appleby and Constance Zimmer, the show focuses on the moral and emotional fallout when producers manufacture storylines and manipulate contestants to drive ratings. Blending sharp workplace drama with media critique and black humor, the series examines themes of exploitation, authenticity, power, and mental health while maintaining a tense, character-driven emotional tone. Through claustrophobic backstage scenes and glossy on-camera contrasts, it exposes the human cost of entertainment and the ethical compromises behind televised spectacle.
properties.plot_summary: Inside the production of a hit dating-competition series, producers and executives systematically manufacture conflict, romance, and spectacle to maximize ratings. A junior producer finds herself both complicit in and tormented by the ethical compromises required to shape contestants into storylines, while a ruthless executive producer exerts ruthless creative control to keep the show commercially viable. Behind the cameras, friendships fracture, manipulations escalate, and the distinction between performance and genuine feeling blurs as staffers exploit emotional vulnerabilities for narrative payoff. The series probes the emotional toll on contestants and crew, exposing how a glossy television product is fabricated through deception, power plays, and personal sacrifice.

properties.description: Black Mirror, created by Charlie Brooker and first released in 2011, is a British anthology television series that presents standalone near-future dramas exploring the societal and personal costs of technology. Each episode functions as a self-contained film combining elements of drama, science fiction, mystery and thriller, and frequently uses satire and moral irony to interrogate themes such as surveillance, social media, privacy and human frailty. The series features a rotating cast across episodes, including performers such as Anjana Vasan, Cristin Milioti and Jimmi Simpson, and is notable for its unsettling atmosphere and thought-provoking twists. Overall, the show aims to provoke reflection and unease about plausible technological developments and their ethical consequences.
properties.plot_summary: An anthology of standalone episodes set in near-future or alternate-present worlds, each dramatizing a different way technology reshapes everyday life and human relationships. Stories range from intimate character studies to high-concept thought experiments, often ending with a moral or ironic twist. Episodes adopt satirical and suspenseful tones to probe privacy, surveillance, social status, and the unintended consequences of innovation. Across its episodes the series foregrounds ordinary people confronted with ethically fraught choices that reveal larger social anxieties.

properties.description: Electric Dreams (2017) is a ten-episode science-fiction anthology inspired by the short fiction of Philip K. Dick. Produced as episodic adaptations, each installment is directed and acted by a rotating creative team and a changing ensemble cast, and the show blends science fiction, dystopian, and psychological-thriller sensibilities. Across its standalone stories the series stages speculative scenarios that probe technology’s social impact, the fragility of identity, surveillance and privacy, and ethical dilemmas about humanity and morality. Tonally restrained but often unsettling, the show favors cinematic visuals and concept-driven plots that reward reflective, intellectually curious viewers.
properties.plot_summary: A ten-episode anthology that adapts separate short stories and novelettes into standalone, self-contained dramas set across a range of near-future and far-future worlds. Each episode presents a speculative scenario — from oppressive, paranoid policing systems to societies reshaped by omnipresent surveillance, consumer tech that warps relationships, and altered or replicated selves — and follows characters forced to confront the ethical, existential, and social consequences of advanced technology. Episodes focus tightly on a small cast, building tension through moral dilemmas, identity crises, and disorienting twists that examine what it means to be human in environments that stretch memory, agency, and privacy to their breaking points.

properties.description: Memories of the Alhambra (2018) is a South Korean drama-thriller that blends romance and science-fiction; it was created by writer Song Jae-jung and directed by Ahn Gil-ho, starring Hyun Bin, Park Shin-hye and Min Jin-woong. The story follows an investor who, after a professional betrayal, travels to Spain and becomes embroiled with a hostel owner in a mysterious augmented-reality game whose glitches begin to affect the real world. The series uses the setting of Granada and motifs drawn from the Alhambra to explore themes of trust, obsession, and the ethical risks of immersive technology, delivering a tense, unpredictable emotional tone.
properties.plot_summary: After a professional betrayal, investor Yoo Jin-woo travels to Spain for a business meeting and takes up lodging at an aging hostel run by former classical guitarist Jung Hee-joo. Their stay becomes the center of a mysterious incident tied to an immersive augmented-reality game whose glitches begin to affect the real world. As the boundaries between game and reality blur, alliances shift and obsessions deepen, forcing both to confront betrayal, trust, and the costs of technological ambition.

properties.description: Humans (2015) is a British-American science fiction drama that stars Katherine Parkinson, Gemma Chan, and Lucy Carless. Set in a near-present parallel world, the series centers on humanoid synthetic servants known as 'Synths' and the cascading personal and societal consequences when some begin to exhibit self-awareness. Blending intimate family drama with broader ethical and political questions, the show interrogates consciousness, personhood, labor displacement, and the emotional costs of technological dependence. Its tone is dark, reflective, and emotionally charged, combining philosophical inquiry with suspenseful storytelling.
properties.plot_summary: In a near-present parallel world, highly developed humanoid servants known as 'Synths' have become commonplace in domestic life. When a middle-class family acquires a Synth, the apparent convenience of perfectly obedient machines collides with emergent questions of consciousness, rights, and identity. As Synths begin to display unexpected self-awareness, intimate family dramas escalate into broader social and economic conflicts. The series explores the moral, philosophical, and emotional consequences of living alongside beings that look human but challenge what it means to be one.

properties.description: High Maintenance (HBO debut 2016) is an American anthology comedy-drama created and principally directed by Ben Sinclair and Katja Blichfeld. Ben Sinclair stars as the central courier figure often credited simply as “The Guy,” who delivers cannabis across Brooklyn and connects a rotating cast of clients in short, character-focused episodes. The series — born from an earlier Vimeo web series and expanded into a half-hour HBO format — blends comedy and drama in vignette-style stories that function as character studies and a portrait of urban life. Across its episodes the show explores themes of loneliness, boredom, human connection, and the quotidian details that reveal deeper emotional truths, adopting a naturalistic, intimate tone that is at once wry and quietly moving. It foregrounds observational storytelling, diverse perspectives, and an ensemble of guest performers drawn from the New York theater and screen community.
properties.plot_summary: A cannabis courier navigates Brooklyn neighborhoods making deliveries while acting as a quiet, connecting presence in the lives of the people he meets. Each episode focuses on one or more clients — strangers, friends, couples, and loners — presenting a short, self-contained vignette that reveals private struggles, small joys, and awkward intimacies. The courier’s rounds provide entry points into these characters’ apartments and routines, and the episodes together build a mosaic of urban life through moments of humor, embarrassment, tenderness, and melancholy. The series privileges character detail and atmosphere over plot mechanics, using the courier as the through-line that ties otherwise independent portraits of New Yorkers into an interconnected urban tapestry.
properties.filming_location: New York City, New York, USA
properties.genre_description: A character-driven comedy-drama presented in an anthology (vignette) format, the show blends slice-of-life realism with episodic storytelling. It fits within urban drama and character study subgenres, using short, self-contained episodes to examine ordinary people and relationships rather than relying on serialized plot arcs. The balance of comedic and dramatic moments places it within the dramedy tradition.
properties.style_description: Naturalistic and intimate in visual approach, the show favors unobtrusive direction, handheld or lightly mobile camerawork, and close-up compositions that emphasize actors’ performances and domestic interiors. Episodes are vignette-style and observational, often feeling like short films centered on a single character or moment. Sound and music choices are restrained, reinforcing the authentic, slice-of-life atmosphere rather than dramatic manipulation.

properties.plot_themes_description: The series repeatedly explores the ways individual lives intersect in a dense city: chance connections, emotional isolation, and the mundane rituals that structure daily existence. It examines the human condition through brief, intimate encounters that foreground loneliness, longing, boredom, and empathy, while also highlighting diversity of lifestyle, class, and background. properties.emotional_tone_description: The tone is quietly empathetic and observational, balancing gentle humor with moments of melancholy. properties.description: Chef's Table is a 2015 Netflix documentary series created and directed by David Gelb. The program profiles world-renowned chefs in hour-long cinematic episodes that blend formal interviews, archival footage and beautifully shot sequences of kitchens, markets and landscapes. Early episodes feature chefs such as Massimo Bottura, Dan Barber, Francis Mallmann, Niki Nakayama, Ben Shewry and Magnus Nilsson, and subsequent seasons expand to chefs from diverse geographies and traditions. Combining biography and food reportage, the series investigates the creative impulses, cultural roots and personal sacrifices behind culinary innovation, delivered in a contemplative, artful tone that emphasizes sensory detail and emotional depth.
properties.plot_summary: The series moves beyond recipes to immerse viewers in the personal and professional worlds of individual, world-class chefs. Each episode focuses on a single chef’s origins, influences, ambitions and struggles, tracing how family, place, memory and culture shape their culinary vision. Lush cinematography and slow, sensory editing emphasize the artistry of ingredients, technique and plating while interweaving intimate interviews, archival material and scenes from the kitchen and dining room. Over time the portraits illuminate broader questions about creativity, tradition versus innovation, sustainability, and the emotional costs and rewards of pursuing excellence in food.
properties.genre_description: A documentary series in the profile-driven subgenre of culinary documentary: episodes function as nonfiction character studies centered on chefs and gastronomy. Stylistically it uses observational and interview-based documentary techniques combined with stylized cinematography and sound design to investigate cultural practices, creative processes and artisanal skill within the world of food.
properties.style_description: Visually sumptuous and deliberately paced, the series employs high-production cinematography, tight macro shots of food, elegant lighting, and careful composition to create a poetic, immersive experience. properties.description: The Girlfriend Experience (2016) is an American anthology drama executive produced by Steven Soderbergh and directed in part by Lodge Kerrigan, Amy Seimetz and Anja Marquardt. properties.plot_summary: Across three self-contained seasons, the series follows different women who navigate worlds where intimacy, commerce and ambition collide. Each season centers on a protagonist who adopts escorting—initially as a pragmatic, high-end transaction—and finds that the work exposes and reshapes her ambitions, relationships and sense of self. One arc follows a law student who moonlights as an elite escort while trying to reconcile her emerging professional identity with the secrecy and compromises of her double life. A later season follows a neuroscience student who becomes entwined with tech start-ups and the London escort scene, using both worlds to test boundaries of control, data and desire. properties.description: Genius (2017) is an anthology biographical drama produced for National Geographic that presents season-long dramatizations of major historical figures. A later season charts a singer’s journey from church choirs to international stardom, illuminating the crafting of an iconic voice amid family, faith, and industry pressures.
